rule: Top-level / file-level code (outside any function or type): the caller is the file's module ID. Languages with a module qualifier use it (Python module, JS/TS module, Lua module, OCaml/Haskell module, Rust module path `crate::a::b`, Groovy `pkg.Script#run`). Languages without one (Ruby, PHP, C, C++, ObjC, Zig file scope) use the file path below the scan root without extension (`lib/devise/rails/routes`). An empty caller or `<global>` is a wrong caller. Free function: its name (with the language's module qualifier where it has one).
notes: Top-level code in bin/setup.rb has caller `bin/setup` (Ruby has no module qualifier: file path below the scan root without extension). A top-level `def` is a free function: its bare name `banner` (Ruby has no qualifier), high from both the top level and from inside Installer#install (it is not a member of Installer; it resolves to the scanned free function). `.install` is on a call result -> computed, low.
